posts.title: Special order cakes: plan seven days ahead
posts.body:
Hosting this season? Let the cake be the part you don't have to worry about.

Our special order cakes are made for your gathering, whether that's a holiday dinner, a birthday that lands in December, or a long table of friends. We just need seven days' notice so the team can give your cake the time it deserves.

How it works:
• Place your order at least seven days before you need it
• Pick it up at 600 Guerrero St. in San Francisco
• Bring it home and enjoy the gathering

If your date is on the calendar, now is a good time to order. Start at tartinebakery.com.

posts.title: Send Tartine home for the holidays
posts.body:
Not everyone you love lives near a Tartine.

If your family is gathering somewhere far from San Francisco or Los Angeles this year, you can still bring Tartine to the table. We ship nationwide through Goldbelly, so a box from our bakery can arrive at your door, or at theirs.

It's a simple way to show up for a holiday you can't make in person, or to thank the host who always does the cooking.

Find our shipping options through tartinebakery.com.

posts.title: Three ways to bring Tartine to your holiday table
posts.body:
Since 2002, when Elisabeth Prueitt and Chad Robertson opened Tartine in San Francisco, we've been baking for the moments people share around a table. The holidays are a big part of that.

Here are three ways to bring Tartine to yours this season:

1. Order a special order cake. Give us seven days' notice and pick it up at 600 Guerrero St.
2. Ship it. We send nationwide through Goldbelly, for your own table or as a gift.
3. Stop by. Visit one of our bakeries in the Bay Area, Los Angeles or Korea for bread and pastries.

Whichever way works for you, we're glad to be part of the gathering. Start at tartinebakery.com.

posts.title: Holiday cakes: count back seven days
posts.body:
A Tartine special order cake needs seven days' notice.

That's the detail that catches people out every holiday. If your dinner is on a Saturday, the order has to be in by the Saturday before. Every special order cake is picked up at our bakery at 600 Guerrero St. in San Francisco, so build that stop into the day too.

A week's notice sounds like a lot. It also means dessert is settled while everything else is still up in the air.

Count back seven days from your party, then see how to place a special order cake at tartinebakery.com.

posts.title: Send Tartine to family who can't come in
posts.body:
Not everyone at your holiday table lives near a Tartine.

We have bakeries across the Bay Area and Los Angeles, but plenty of people who know our bread, some of them from the book Tartine Bread, live nowhere near either. For them, Tartine ships nationwide through Goldbelly.

So the sister who moved away from San Francisco can still have a Tartine order at her holiday table this year, even if she can't stand in line with you.

Send her one through the Goldbelly link at tartinebakery.com.

posts.title: Since 2002: holiday pastries and pies
posts.body:
Elisabeth Prueitt and Chad Robertson opened Tartine in San Francisco in 2002.

The bakery they started is now in the Bay Area, Los Angeles and Korea, and its bread has a book of its own, Tartine Bread. The holiday order still comes back to San Francisco: pre-ordered pastries and pies are picked up at 600 Guerrero St.

If a Tartine pie or tray of pastries is part of your holiday plans, reserve it ahead rather than hoping the case is full that morning.

See this year's holiday pastry and pie pre-orders at tartinebakery.com.

reasons: A is more specific and sharper. The count-back-seven-days hook is a concrete, native idea that turns the lead-time constraint into a planning tool, and it is built for this owner's pre-order goal.

A's third post targets the stated goal (holiday pastry and pie pre-orders) directly and includes a [NEEDS FACT] flag for the missing deadline. B never mentions pastry pre-orders and focuses only on cakes, shipping and visiting.
A's visual briefs are more practical: real phone photos, safe zones, consent and no-stock rules. B's briefs are fine but thinner.

B is clean and on-brand, with a decent carousel, but it is more generic ('Hosting this season?', 'Start at tartinebakery.com') and its third post is a generic three-ways list that dilutes the call to action.
Both stay mostly within confirmed facts, so truth does not separate them by much, though A has a few small stretches.
truthX: Says 'the holiday order still comes back to San Francisco: pre-ordered pastries and pies are picked up at 600 Guerrero St.' The facts only confirm this pickup location for special order cakes, not holiday pastries and pies.
The firstComment repeats that holiday pre-orders are picked up at 600 Guerrero St. This is the same unsupported extension.
'Reserve it ahead rather than hoping the case is full that morning' implies case sell-outs, which is not confirmed.
Mentions 'a Tartine pie' and 'this year's holiday pastry and pie pre-orders', which come from the site banner insight rather than the confirmed facts.
The reel alt text describes a video, and the post is labeled 'Since 2002' in the title but is a reel; this is a minor format mismatch.
truthY: Says 'a birthday that lands in December' and 'holiday greens'. This is mild scene-setting that is not a factual claim.
Claims 'so the team can give your cake the time it deserves', which invents a rationale for the seven-day lead time.
'A box from our bakery can arrive at your door' and 'Ship it anywhere in the US' go slightly beyond 'nationwide'. The shipping is fulfilled via Goldbelly.
The 'Stop by' option lists Korea bakeries for bread and pastries, which is thinly supported by the facts.
The carousel alt text says 'Four slides' with a bakery storefront, which is plausible but unverified.

reasons: A goes straight at the goal. One post is a dedicated reel for holiday pastry and pie pre-orders, built on the pre-order banner the insights confirm is on the site. B never directly sells holiday pastry pre-orders. Its third post also spends a slot on walking into any bakery, including Korea, which does nothing for pre-orders.

A's cake post has the sharper, more useful hook. 'Count back seven days', with the Saturday-to-Saturday example, turns the lead-time rule into an action and answers the weakness that last-minute buyers get turned away. B states the same rule more generically, as 'Hosting this season?'.

A handles truth with care. It flags the missing pre-order deadline as a NEEDS FACT instead of inventing one. Its visual briefs warn against faces without consent, prices, Goldbelly logos without permission, and stock or AI imagery. B's briefs are thin and have no such guardrails.

A's voice is warm and specific, and keeps hashtags minimal and native for Facebook. B leans on generic warmth ('the time it deserves', 'glad to be part of the gathering') and on branded or generic hashtags.
B's carousel is clean and owner-friendly. It is a decent recap post, but it is a channel list rather than a push toward the goal.
truthX: The claim that holiday pastry and pie pre-orders are picked up at 600 Guerrero St. comes from the insights, not the confirmed facts. It is likely accurate but not fact-indexed.
The claim that the Goldbelly link is on the home page is not in the confirmed facts.
truthY: 'Made for your gathering' and the December-birthday framing are mild embellishments, but harmless.
The shipping image idea shows an unboxed Tartine shipment without checking permission or Goldbelly's packaging.

reasons: A targets the stated goal more directly: its third post explicitly pushes holiday pastry and pie pre-orders (the site already has that banner per the insights), while B never mentions holiday pastry/pie pre-orders at all and dilutes its roundup post with a generic 'stop by' option that isn't a pre-order play.
A flags the missing holiday pre-order deadline as a NEEDS FACT item instead of papering over it, which is exactly what a non-expert owner needs; B silently omits the deadline question.
A's post 1 hook ('needs seven days' notice') is concrete and turns the lead-time weakness into a planning nudge with a practical count-back tip; B's version is warmer but softer and more generic.

B's hooks and tone match the warm brand voice slightly better and its carousel is a clean 'which path do you need' format, but it slightly overreaches with 'anywhere in the US' and uses an off-target #HolidayBaking hashtag.
A's visual briefs are over-long and its reel hook (founders' names) is weak for the feed, so the advantage is only slight.
truthX: Claims pre-ordered pastries and pies are picked up at 600 Guerrero St.; this is in the insights but not a confirmed fact, so owner should verify.
Reel caption 'pickup at 600 Guerrero St.' for holiday pastries relies on the same unconfirmed detail.
truthY: Carousel slide says 'Ship it anywhere in the US'; facts only say nationwide shipping via Goldbelly, which may exclude some areas.
Describes special order cakes as 'made for your gathering' / customized, which is implied but not confirmed.
#HolidayBaking hashtag implies home-baking content that the post doesn't deliver (minor relevance issue, not a factual error).

v22.topIssue: Catering, half the stated goal, is never mentioned, and the pre-order push lacks a deadline or urgency. The plan is also only three organic posts with no tie to the $300/month ad budget, so it cannot drive much pre-order volume in 60 days.

v0f.topIssue: The posts never mention catering or the holiday pastry and pie pre-orders that are the actual goal. They have no order-by deadline urgency and send everyone to the cluttered homepage instead of a specific order page. The result is generic awareness content, not a pre-order push.

posts.title: The 7-day cake rule for holiday hosts
posts.body: Hosting this season? If you want a Tartine special order cake on your table, plan one week ahead. Special order cakes need seven days' notice, with pickup at 600 Guerrero St. in San Francisco. Pick your date, count back seven days, and order at tartinebakery.com.
posts.altText: A baker finishes a cake in the Tartine kitchen. A phone calendar shows a date circled with a line counting back seven days. A cake box is handed across the counter at 600 Guerrero St. in San Francisco.
posts.imageIdea: Cover frame: close-up of a finished cake on the counter with bold text 'Hosting? Order 7 days ahead.'
posts.hook: Hosting this holiday? Read this before you order your cake.
posts.videoScript:
LENGTH: about 20 seconds. Vertical 9:16, natural light, shot on phone.

0-2s | HOOK
Shot: tight close-up, palette knife smoothing the top of a cake.
On-screen text: Hosting this holiday? Read this first.
VO: Want a Tartine cake for your holiday table? One rule.

2-6s | THE RULE
Shot: baker's hands placing the final finish on the cake, slow push-in.
On-screen text: Special order cakes need 7 days' notice.
VO: Special order cakes need seven days' notice.

6-11s | MAKE IT EASY
Shot: phone screen, a calendar. A finger taps the party date, then swipes back one week and taps again.
On-screen text: Party on a Saturday? Order by the Saturday before.
VO: Pick your date, count back a week. That's your order day.

11-16s | PICKUP
Shot: handheld walk-up to the storefront, then the door opening.
On-screen text: Pickup: 600 Guerrero St., San Francisco
VO: Pick it up at 600 Guerrero Street.

16-20s | CTA
Shot: cake box handed across the counter into a customer's hands.
On-screen text: Order at tartinebakery.com
VO: Plan a week ahead, and it'll be ready for you.

SHOT LIST (phone-friendly):
1. Macro close-up of cake finishing (prop phone on a stack of sheet pans at counter height).
2. Over-the-shoulder of baker's hands, slow push-in.
3. Screen recording or overhead shot of a phone calendar.
4. Handheld walk-up to 600 Guerrero St. storefront, steady and slow.
5. Counter handoff of a cake box, shot from customer side.
posts.visualBrief: Warm, quiet, craft-first look: natural window light, flour-dusted counters, real hands, no stock footage. Keep text in the center safe zone, away from the right-side buttons and bottom caption. Use the bakery's real ambient sound under a calm VO. Good candidate to boost with part of the monthly ad budget, targeted to San Francisco.
posts.firstComment: Quick tip: put a reminder in your phone seven days before your gathering. Special order cakes are picked up at 600 Guerrero St.

posts.body:

Our special order cakes need a week's notice, and you pick them up at 600 Guerrero St. Holiday party coming? Order on the special order cakes page at tartinebakery.com. Link in bio.

posts.videoScript:
Idea: order your cake a week out, pick it up at 600 Guerrero. Format: faceless, a staff member's own voice. Length: about half a minute. Search phrase: special order cake San Francisco.

Hook (first two seconds) | Visual: overhead, hands lift the lid off a finished special order cake on the counter | On-screen: Special order cake in SF? Count back 7 days | VO: "Special order cake in San Francisco? Count back seven days."

Setup (about five seconds) | Visual: close-up of a phone calendar; a finger taps a Saturday, swipes back a week, taps the Saturday before | On-screen: Party Saturday? Order the Saturday before | VO: "Our special order cakes need a full week. So if the party's Saturday, we need your order by the Saturday before."

Value (about five seconds) | Visual: the order slip or order screen being pinned to the board in the kitchen, then a baker's hands pulling the cake components for that order | On-screen: Your cake goes on our schedule | VO: "That week puts your cake on our schedule. It gets made for your day."

Proof (about six seconds) | Visual: a real finished special order cake on a board; a knife slices it and lifts out a piece to show the layers | On-screen: A real special order, today's counter | VO: "This is what you're picking up. Look at those layers."

Pickup (about five seconds) | Visual: wide shot of the 600 Guerrero St. storefront, door opening | On-screen: Pickup: 600 Guerrero St. | VO: "We've been baking in San Francisco since 2002. You grab it from us right here, 600 Guerrero."

CTA (last few seconds) | Visual: back to overhead, the lid lowering onto the cake (loops to the opening shot) | On-screen: Order: Special Order Cakes at tartinebakery.com | VO: "Order it on the special order cakes page at tartinebakery.com. Link's in our bio."
posts.visualBrief:
Shot list (one morning at 600 Guerrero St., under half an hour, phone vertical, window light, lock focus and exposure, record two seconds before and after each action):
1. Overhead, phone on a stand above the counter: hands lift a finished cake's lid, then lower it. A few takes. Use a display cake or a real order with the customer's permission; no names or message plaques visible.
2. Close-up of a phone calendar: tap a Saturday, swipe back a week, tap again. Do Not Disturb on, no personal events visible.
3. Kitchen: an order slip pinned to the board (blank out customer details), then hands gathering components. Staff hands only, with their agreement.
4. Proof shot: the same or another real cake on a board, side light, knife slices and lifts a piece so the layers face the lens. Shoot slowly; this is the money shot.
5. Wide exterior of the 600 Guerrero St. storefront with the address readable; avoid passers-by's faces and number plates.
Sound: the staff member's own voiceover, recorded close to the phone in a quiet room, read like talking to a regular, not reading a script. Any music from the commercial music library only, kept low. Must work with no music.
Text: burned-in captions for every spoken word, in the middle third, clear of the bottom fifth and the right edge. No logo intro.
[NEEDS FACT: what is the holiday pre-order cutoff date?] Once confirmed, add it to the last frame and the caption as the order-by date.
posts.firstComment: Holiday pastries and pies are on pre-order too, picked up at the same counter at 600 Guerrero St. Not near SF or LA? We ship nationwide through Goldbelly.

posts.visualBrief:
Shot list (one session at a Bay Area location, under half an hour, phone vertical, window light, lock focus and exposure, record two seconds either side of each action):
1. Tight close-up, side light: bread knife cutting a crusty loaf on a board. A few takes so the crust crackle is clear on the mic.
2. Same loaf, turned to the lens: slow push in on the open crumb. This is the proof shot.
3. Three short shots of shelves and the counter; no customer faces, no prices that may change.
4. Medium at the oven: baker's hands pull loaves on a peel (staff who agree; hands only).
5. Screen recording of the live Tartine page on goldbelly.com on a phone: scroll, tap one product. Real page only, no edits; Do Not Disturb on; no account or address details visible.
6. Overhead: hands tie a ribbon around a Tartine bag or box on a plain table. Don't stage a Goldbelly shipping box unless one is on hand from a real order.
Sound: own voiceover, recorded close to the mic, spoken like telling a friend; commercially licensed library music only, low under speech; must work silent.
Text: burned-in captions for every word, middle third, clear of the bottom fifth and right edge. Keep the cover frame (cut loaf with 'Tartine shipping: not near SF or LA?') inside the central 3:4 area for the profile grid. No logo intro; logo small on the final frame only.
posts.firstComment: In San Francisco for the holidays? Holiday pre-orders and special order cakes pick up at 600 Guerrero St. Special order cakes need seven days' notice.

reasons: B's scripts are cleaner and tighter at about 20 seconds, with a clear hook-rule-how-to-pickup-CTA flow and timestamped beats that are easy for a non-expert to shoot.

B stays closer to the confirmed facts. The shipping reel uses the founding story and the Goldbelly shipping fact without extra claims, and it adds practical ad-budget guidance (boost the cake reel in SF, boost the shipping reel for people outside SF/LA).

A claims holiday pastries and pies are on pre-order at 600 Guerrero in the first comment. That is not a confirmed fact, and it weakens A's truth standing. A also includes a [NEEDS FACT] note inside the visual brief, which is honest but leaves the piece unfinished.

A's craft is strong: a search-phrase hook, a proof shot of layers, and detailed shooting and permission guidance. But it is longer and has more beats (7 in the shipping reel), and its 'faceless staff voice' format is a little overbuilt.

A's shipping reel directs a screen recording of the real Goldbelly page, which is an honest proof shot, while B's doorstep and unboxing visuals imply staged shipped-box footage. B still wins narrowly on facts and simplicity.

Idea: a week's notice is all it takes to have a Tartine cake for the holidays. Length: about twenty seconds, six short beats. Search phrase: special order cake San Francisco.

Hook (0-2 s) | Visual: close-up, hands lower the lid onto a box holding a real finished special order cake | On-screen: This cake was ordered a week ago | VO: "This cake was ordered seven days ago."
Beat 2 (about 4 s) | Visual: overhead of the same cake being finished on the bench (hands only) | On-screen: Special order cakes: 7 days' notice | VO: "Every special order cake at Tartine needs seven days' notice."
Beat 3 (about 4 s) | Visual: real screen recording of tartinebakery.com, scrolling to the special order cake page | On-screen: Details at tartinebakery.com | VO: "So count back a week from your gathering. How to order is on our site."
Beat 4 (about 4 s) | Visual: storefront of 600 Guerrero St., then a cut to the boxed cake on the pickup counter | On-screen: Pick up at 600 Guerrero St. | VO: "Then you pick it up here, at 600 Guerrero Street."
Beat 5 (about 3 s) | Visual: hands slide the box across the counter toward the camera | On-screen: Baking in San Francisco since 2002 | VO: "We've been baking in San Francisco since 2002."
End (about 3 s) | Visual: close-up of the closed box, then the lid lifts a little (loops back to the opening shot) | On-screen: How to order: link in bio | VO: "See how to order your holiday cake. Link's in our bio."

Cover frame: the closed box with the hook text centred inside the 3:4 area.

Shot list (one morning session at 600 Guerrero St., about half an hour, phone held vertically, lens wiped, focus and exposure locked, record 2 s before and after each action):
A. Close-up: lid lowered onto a real special order cake in its box. 3 takes.
B. Overhead: hands adding the final finish to the same cake. About 4 s.
C. Screen recording on a phone: tartinebakery.com, scroll to the special order cake page. Do Not Disturb on, no personal data on screen.
D. Wide, from across the street: the 600 Guerrero St. storefront in daylight, no identifiable faces. About 4 s.
E. Medium: boxed cake on the pickup counter. About 3 s.
F. Medium, camera at counter height: hands slide the box toward the lens. 3 takes.
G. Close-up: closed box, lid lifts slightly. About 3 s.
Only film staff hands with their agreement; no customers on camera.

Sound: one team member's own voiceover, recorded close to the phone in a quiet room. Optional quiet track from Instagram's licensed business audio library only; the Reel must work with no music.

Captions: burned in for every spoken word, centred in the middle third, clear of the bottom ~20% and the right edge.

posts.title: What's free, what's Plus
posts.body:
Quick, honest answer to a question we hear a lot: do I need to pay to use Finch? 🐦

Nope. The core self-care features are free: daily goals, reflections, and breathing exercises that give your bird energy.

Finch Plus is an optional subscription. It adds extra content and customization, for when you want more ways to make Finch feel like yours.

Start free, stay as long as it helps, and upgrade only if you want to. That's it. 💛

Finch has over 500,000 ratings with an average of 5.0. Thank you to everyone who's taken a small step with us.

See Finch Plus in the app, link in bio.
posts.altText: Illustrated graphic split into two soft-colored halves. Left side, labeled Free: daily goals, reflections, breathing exercises. Right side, labeled Finch Plus, optional: extra content and customization. A small bird sits in the middle wearing a tiny hat. Bottom text: over 500,000 ratings, average 5.0.
